Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
# HTTP benchmark of a Ts.ED server (Express, Koa, Fastify, fulmine.js):
# - after each stable release: the reference version vs the released one (shown on tsed.dev/benchmarks);
# - manually, with the list of targets to compare (published versions and/or "local");
# - on a pull request when the "benchmark" label is added: base branch vs PR head.
# Every target of a comparison is measured in this single job. See tools/benchmarks/readme.md.
name: Benchmark

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      targets:
        description: "Comma-separated targets, the first one is the baseline (e.g. 8.44.1,8.44.12 or 8.44.12,local). Empty: latest release vs local"
        required: false
        default: ""
      platforms:
        description: "Platforms to measure"
        required: false
        default: "express,koa,fastify,fulmine"
      rounds:
        description: "Interleaved rounds (more rounds narrow the confidence interval)"
        required: false
        default: "5"
      duration:
        description: "Measured seconds per route and round"
        required: false
        default: "5"
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ts.ED version before the performance work, compared with each release.
  # Keep it in sync with REFERENCE_VERSION of BenchmarksService in tsedio/tsed-cms.
  REFERENCE_VERSION: "8.44.1"

jobs:
  benchmark:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'benchmark' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && !github.event.release.prerelease)
    # at the job level, so that adding another label to the PR does not cancel a running benchmark
    concurrency:
      group: benchmark-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # the PR head itself, not the merge commit GitHub checks out by default on pull_request
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          path: head
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Checkout the base branch
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          path: base
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Use Node.js 24.18.0
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24.18.0
          cache: "yarn"
          cache-dependency-path: head/yarn.lock

      - name: Resolve the targets
        id: targets
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          INPUT_TARGETS: ${{ inputs.targets }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          if [ "$EVENT" = "pull_request" ]; then
            targets="local-base,local-head"
          elif [ "$EVENT" = "release" ]; then
            targets="$REFERENCE_VERSION,${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
          elif [ -n "$INPUT_TARGETS" ]; then
            targets="$INPUT_TARGETS"
          else
            targets="$(npm view @tsed/core version),local"
          fi
          echo "targets=$targets" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Targets: $targets"

      # the release event can arrive before the packages are visible on the npm registry, and a release can stop halfway:
      # wait for every package the bench app installs (their

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check

Bound jobs with a custom timeout

Pattern: P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (job_timeout)

When is bound jobs with a custom timeout applicable?

Assess bound jobs with a custom timeout for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Representative successful-duration history exists

Contraindications: Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit

Method: Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom; Measure false timeout failures separately

Reported finding: Custom timeouts reduce runaway consumption.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 12.9, "paid": 8.1}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.6; Table 4; PDF pp. 7, 8: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf
